dedupe_keys.name: plegma greek household appliance electricity and context

description: Plegma Labs, NTUA and the University of Strathclyde publish electricity and contextual observations from 13 Greek households. Aggregate and appliance measurements have ten-second resolution, with indoor temperature and humidity, building characteristics and user-practice information. The university repository lists 218 million readings and provides raw and cleaned CSV collections in 7z archives, free under CC BY 4.0. Its coverage field starts in July 2022, while the production dates and GitHub README start in September 2022; both end in September 2023. The data can calibrate household demand and appliance-control simulations alongside model-energyplus and model-pypsa. A caveat is that gaps, repairs and meter discrepancies are present, and the small household sample is not nationally representative. A published correction replaces Figure 10 percentages in the descriptor. No archive contents were downloaded.
